root_cause.text: The `ti-adc161s626` IIO ADC driver passed stack-allocated temporary buffers to `spi_read()`, but SPI transfers require DMA-safe memory, so the driver could trigger unsafe DMA access when reading measurements.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `__be16 buf`/`__be32 buf` on the stack with `data->buf[3] __aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN)` and changes `spi_read(data->spi, (void *) &buf, ...)` to `spi_read(data->spi, data->buf, ...)`, while the commit message explicitly states “All SPI buffers must be DMA-safe.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the unaligned-access helper header needed for safe handling of unaligned data.
intent_record.what: A new include directive, `#include <linux/unaligned.h>`, was added to the header list.
intent_record.how: This makes unaligned memory access helper functions/macros available to the file at compile time, enabling code in the translation unit to safely read or write packed or unaligned values without relying on implicit declarations or manual handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a DMA-aligned internal buffer to `ti_adc_data` to support safe ADC data reads.
intent_record.what: A new member `u8 buf[3] __aligned(IIO_DMA_MINALIGN);` was added to `struct ti_adc_data` immediately after the existing `read_size` and `shift` fields.
intent_record.how: This gives the driver a small, DMA-aligned 3-byte buffer inside the device state structure, likely for staging ADC read data in a way that satisfies DMA alignment requirements and avoids unaligned accesses or buffer placement issues at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix ti_adc measurement reads to use an unaligned-safe buffer and conversion helpers for 2-byte and 3-byte SPI transfers.
intent_record.what: In ti_adc_read_measurement(), the temporary stack buffers for 2-byte and 3-byte SPI reads were removed. Both switch cases now read directly into data->buf via spi_read(), and the conversion now uses get_unaligned_be16(data->buf) for 2-byte values and get_unaligned_be24(data->buf) for 3-byte values instead of be16_to_cpu()/be32_to_cpu() on local __be16/__be32 variables.
intent_record.how: This changes the read path to use a shared buffer that can safely hold potentially unaligned SPI data, avoiding reliance on stack-allocated typed objects that may not be suitably aligned for direct byte-wise DMA/SPI writes. Functionally, it still returns the same numeric measurement values, but it is more robust on architectures that fault on unaligned accesses or when the SPI core writes into arbitrary memory.

The changes directly address the root cause by replacing stack-allocated SPI read buffers with a DMA-safe internal buffer and using conversion helpers for the ADC transfer formats.

This also passes a stack-allocated temporary buffer to spi_read(), creating the same DMA-unsafe access path when reading 3-byte measurements.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `ti_adc_read_measurement()`. For both SPI transfer sizes it uses stack-allocated temporaries and passes them directly to `spi_read()`: `__be16 buf; ret = spi_read(data->spi, (void *) &buf, 2);` and `__be32 buf; ret = spi_read(data->spi, (void *) &buf, 3);`. This matches the root cause: stack buffers are being used as SPI DMA targets, which is unsafe because SPI transfers require DMA-safe memory. There is no fix here (no DMA-safe staging buffer, no `spi_read_then_*` alternative, no allocation with `kmalloc`, etc.), so `is_fixed` is false. The snippet is sufficient because the problematic read path is fully shown.
